title: What If You Walked Blindfolded Across a Desert? You'd Circle

scenes.text: What if you tried to walk in a straight line with no landmarks? You couldn't, scientists found.
Researchers sent volunteers walking for hours in the Sahara and a German forest, tracked by GPS.
When the Sun was visible, they walked fairly straight. When clouds covered it, they started curving.
Blindfolded, some walked in circles less than 20 meters wide. They thought they were going straight.
It isn't one leg being longer. The same person veered left, then right.
Your sense of straight drifts the moment you lose a landmark. The Sun was their guide.

description:
What if you walked in a straight line with no landmarks?
In a Max Planck study, volunteers in the Sahara and a German forest walked in circles whenever the Sun or Moon was hidden, without noticing.
What should we run through next?
